sections.learningObjectives:
- Define common word roots, prefixes, and suffixes of the male and female reproductive systems.
- Build and decode male and female reproductive system terms from their component word parts.
- Recognize common reproductive, gynecologic, and obstetric conditions and procedures by their terminology.
- Distinguish similar-sounding reproductive terms and apply them accurately in documentation and communication.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of 'hyster/o' as the label for the pear-shaped organ where a baby grows. If a word has hyster/o in it, it is talking about the uterus.

### Question 2

The ovaries are the two small egg-holders. 'oophor/o' is the word part that points to them, just like a name tag on a drawer.

### Question 3

The fallopian tubes are the little tunnels an egg travels through. 'salping/o' is the special word for those tunnels.

### Question 4

colp/o is the code word for the birth canal. When a term starts with colp/o, think of the vagina.

### Question 5

mast/o is the word part for the breast. Mamm/o is its twin, like two nicknames for the same thing.

### Question 6

The testes are the two small factories that make sperm. 'orchid/o' is the word part that names them.

### Question 7

The prostate is a walnut-sized gland in men. 'prostat/o' is its name tag, so prostat- words are always about the prostate.

### Question 8

The vas deferens is the tube that carries sperm out. 'vas/o' is the word for that tube, and vasectomy means cutting it.

### Question 9

-rrhagia is a red-alert suffix: it means a lot of bleeding is happening, like a pipe bursting.

### Question 10

-rrhaphy means sewing something back together, like stitching up a torn seam in fabric.

### Question 11

-cyesis is the word for pregnancy itself. It shows up in older medical words for being pregnant.

### Question 12

men/o is the word part for the monthly period. It is the same 'men' as in 'menstrual.'

### Question 13

Break it into pieces: 'a-' means no, 'men/o' means periods, and '-rrhea' means flow. So amenorrhea is when the monthly flow is missing.

### Question 14

'dys-' means painful and 'men/o' means periods. Put them together and dysmenorrhea is just painful periods.

### Question 15

men/o means periods and -rrhagia means a big flow. Menorrhagia is when the period bleeding is way too heavy.

### Question 16

olig/o means 'just a little.' Oligomenorrhea is when periods come rarely or are very light.

### Question 17

The lining that belongs inside the uterus starts growing in places it should not be. That misplaced lining is endometriosis.

### Question 18

The -itis suffix says 'inflamed.' Endometritis is a sore, swollen lining inside the uterus.

### Question 19

hyster/o means uterus and -ectomy means 'take it out.' A hysterectomy removes the uterus.

### Question 20

salping/o is the tube and -ectomy is removal. Salpingectomy takes out a fallopian tube.

### Question 21

oophor/o is the ovary and -ectomy is removal. Oophorectomy removes an ovary.

### Question 22

This long word is two word parts plus 'take out.' It removes a tube and an ovary at the same time.

### Question 23

colposcopy uses a magnifier to look closely at the vagina and cervix, usually after an abnormal Pap result.

### Question 24

hysteroscopy is a tiny camera that looks inside the uterus, like peeking into a small room.

### Question 25

-rrhaphy means stitching. Colporrhaphy sews up a weakened vaginal wall.

### Question 26

The cervix is the doorway of the uterus. Cervicitis means that doorway is sore and swollen.

### Question 27

mast/o is breast and -itis means inflamed. Mastitis is a sore, swollen, sometimes infected breast.

### Question 28

mastectomy removes breast tissue. It is different from mastitis (swelling) and mastalgia (pain).

### Question 29

mammography is a special X-ray picture of the breast, like a photo that looks inside to check for problems.

### Question 30

galact/o means milk and -rrhea means flowing out. Galactorrhea is milk leaking when it should not be.

### Question 31

menarche is the very first period a person ever has. The -arche part means 'beginning.'

### Question 32

menopause is when periods stop for good, usually around middle age. 'Pause' is even inside the word.

### Question 33

mastalgia is just a fancy word for a sore breast. -algia always means pain.

### Question 34

orch/o means testis and -itis means inflamed. Orchitis is a swollen, sore testicle.

### Question 35

orchiectomy takes out a testicle. The -ectomy tells you something is being removed.

### Question 36

-pexy means 'tack it in place.' Orchidopexy moves a testicle down and stitches it where it belongs.

### Question 37

crypt/o means hidden. Cryptorchidism is a testicle that stayed hidden up inside instead of moving down.

### Question 38

The epididymis is the coiled tube sitting on the testicle. Epididymitis means that tube is inflamed.

### Question 39

prostatitis is a sore, swollen prostate. It is inflammation, not cancer and not necessarily enlargement.

### Question 40

prostatectomy removes the prostate. The -ectomy ending always means something is being taken out.

### Question 41

vasectomy snips the tube that carries sperm, so sperm cannot get out. It is a birth-control surgery for men.

### Question 42

balanitis is a sore, swollen tip of the penis. balan/o is the word part for the glans.

### Question 43

hydrocele is a little water balloon of fluid around the testicle. 'Hydro' means water.

### Question 44

varicocele is like varicose veins but in the scrotum. The 'varico' part means swollen veins.

### Question 45

BPH means the prostate has grown too big, but it is not cancer. 'Benign' means not dangerous like cancer is.

### Question 46

TURP is a surgery that trims an overgrown prostate by going in through the urine tube, so no big cut is needed.

### Question 47

Gravida counts pregnancies and para counts births. A first-ever pregnancy is a primigravida.

### Question 48

G is the pregnancy score and P is the birth score. G2 means this is her second pregnancy, whatever the outcome.

### Question 49

ante- means before, intra- means during, and post- means after. Postpartum is the time after the baby arrives.

### Question 50

In a D&C, the doctor gently opens the cervix and scrapes the inside of the uterus to remove tissue.

### Question 51

episiotomy is a small cut at the opening to help the baby come out more easily. -tomy always means cutting.

### Question 52

The placenta is the baby's food delivery pad. In placenta previa, it is parked in the way of the exit door.

### Question 53

-centesis means drawing fluid out with a needle. Amniocentesis takes a little of the fluid around the baby to test it.

### Question 54

cephal/o means head. Cephalic just means the baby is lined up head-down, ready to come out head first.

### Question 55

A C-section is when the doctor makes a cut in the belly to take the baby out instead of a vaginal birth.

### Question 56

A fibroid is a harmless (benign) muscle lump in the uterus. Its fancy name, leiomyoma, literally means smooth-muscle tumor.

### Question 57

These three look alike, but each 'men-' word tells a different story: no flow, too much flow, or flow at the wrong time.

### Question 58

An ectopic pregnancy is a pregnancy growing in the wrong place and it can burst. That is a 'get help right now' situation.

### Question 59

Preeclampsia is like a warning light on the car dashboard during pregnancy. The assistant's job is to tell the doctor right away, not to fix it.

### Question 60

When someone is bleeding a lot and feels faint, that is a 'call the grown-up in charge right now' moment. The assistant gets help fast.

### Question 61

Bleeding long after periods have stopped is a warning sign. The right move is to tell the doctor, not to guess it is fine.

### Question 62

Reading a Pap result is like reading a referee's decision — only the trained professional gets to make the call. The assistant passes the message along.

### Question 63

Choosing a birth control method is a decision for the doctor and patient together. The assistant helps by setting up that conversation, not picking for them.

### Question 64

PSA is a clue, not a verdict. Only the doctor can say what it means, so the assistant passes the question to the doctor.

### Question 65

Heavy bleeding during pregnancy is an emergency siren. The assistant gets the doctor right away and stays close to help.
